title: Eagles vs. Titans Week 2 Preview: 6 Key Questions Answered for BleedingGreenNation Fans
body:
The Philadelphia Eagles will head south this weekend for their first road test of the 2024 season, traveling to Nissan Stadium to face the Tennessee Titans in what promises to be a high‑stakes, sweltering Week 2 showdown. Both clubs entered the opening week with lofty expectations, and the clash in Nashville will be a barometer for how quickly each team can translate preseason hype into on‑field execution. With temperatures projected to climb into the mid‑90s, the heat will be an added variable, testing stamina, play‑calling and depth on both sides of the ball.

Philadelphia’s offensive engine, quarterback Jalen Hurts, is looking to cement his status as a dual‑threat leader after a solid debut against the New York Giants. The Eagles amassed 330 yards passing and 70 yards on the ground, but the 30‑point victory was buoyed by a stout defensive performance that forced three turnovers. Against the Titans, Hurts will need to navigate a defensive front anchored by veteran pass‑rusher Jeff ery Wright and a secondary that excelled in limiting big plays last week. The key question for the Eagles is whether they can sustain their balanced attack in a hostile environment; a quick‑strike passing game could keep the Titans’ defense honest, while a commitment to the run will test the Titans’ front seven, which has struggled to contain power backs in the early season.

The Titans, meanwhile, are eager to rebound from a narrow loss to the New England Patriots that exposed vulnerabilities in their pass protection and secondary coverage. Quarterback Ryan Tannehill, returning from a modest 2023 campaign, will rely heavily on his rapport with rookie wideout Jalin Harper and veteran tight end Logan Thomas to stretch the field. The Titans’ offensive line, led by veteran center Nate Stuart, must improve its pass‑blocking consistency to give Tannehill the time needed to dissect the Eagles’ blitz packages. Defensively, Tennessee will look to leverage its aggressive front seven, which recorded eight sacks in the opening game, to pressure Hurts and force errant throws. The Titans’ secondary, however, remains a concern; they allowed a 40‑yard completion rate of 68% last week, a statistic the Eagles can exploit with quick, precise routes.

Special teams could also tilt the balance in Nashville. The Eagles’ rookie kicker, Cameron Davis, proved reliable in Week 1, converting all three field‑goal attempts, while the Titans’ veteran punter Ryan Stone has a reputation for pinning opponents deep inside their own 20‑yard line. Field position will be a premium in a game where every possession is likely to be hard‑earned under the oppressive heat, making disciplined play and effective kicking all the more critical.

Coaching strategies will be under the microscope as well. Eagles head coach Nick Sirianni has emphasized a flexible, tempo‑driven offense that can adapt on the fly, while Titans’ coach Mike Vrabel is known for his aggressive, blitz‑heavy schemes that aim to disrupt the quarterback’s rhythm. The clash of philosophies—Philadelphia’s adaptable, balanced approach versus Tennessee’s high‑pressure, run‑first mentality—should produce a chess match that tests each coordinator’s ability to read and react in real time.

Looking ahead, the outcome of this Week 2 contest could set the tone for the remainder of the season. A victory for the Eagles would reinforce their status as early frontrunners in the NFC East and provide momentum heading into a pivotal divisional slate. Conversely, a win for the Titans would not only redeem their opening‑week disappointment but also signal that they are a legitimate contender in the AFC South, capable of thriving in adverse conditions. As both teams prepare to battle the heat and each other, fans can expect a gritty, strategic contest that will shape the narrative of the 2024 NFL campaign.
